Quick start

Priyansh Srivastava

Source: vignettes/scMaSigPro.Rmd
scMaSigPro.Rmd

Abstract

scMaSigPro finds genes whose expression changes along pseudotime and differs between the branching paths of a single-cell trajectory. This vignette runs the whole workflow on a small simulated data set, from a SingleCellExperiment to lists of genes, plots and clusters, and checks the genes it finds against the truth of the simulation.

Introduction

A trajectory inference tool orders the cells of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment along a pseudotime and splits them into branching paths, such as the paths from a progenitor to two cell types. scMaSigPro finds the genes whose expression changes along the pseudotime of a path and the genes whose expression differs between paths (Srivastava et al. 2024). It brings the method of the maSigPro package for time-course experiments (Conesa et al. 2006; Nueda et al. 2014) to single cells in two steps:

  1. The cells of each path are pooled into bins along pseudotime, and their counts are added up into pseudo-bulk counts. The bins play the part of the time points of a time-course experiment.
  2. A polynomial generalised linear model in the binned pseudotime, with one set of terms per path, is fitted to the pseudo-bulk counts of each gene, by default with a negative binomial distribution and an offset for the sequencing depth of each bin. The genes whose model is better than a flat line, and the terms that make it so, tell how a gene changes along each path.

This vignette runs these steps on splat.sim, a small data set bundled with the package. The other vignettes go further:

  • Trajectory input: pseudotime and path labels from slingshot, Monocle3 or another tool.
  • Shared root: trajectories whose paths share their first cells.
  • Model and tuning: the model, its settings and how they change the results.
  • maSigPro and the ScMaSigPro class: the object, its accessors and the equivalence with maSigPro.
  • Frequently asked questions.

Installation

scMaSigPro is installed from GitHub with BiocManager, which also installs its Bioconductor dependencies:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("BioBam/scMaSigPro")

The data

splat.sim is a SingleCellExperiment with the counts of 100 genes in 200 cells, simulated with splatter (Zappia et al. 2017) along two paths that start from the same cells. Each cell has a simulated step along its path, which serves as its pseudotime, and the label of its path.

library(scMaSigPro)
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(ggplot2)

data("splat.sim", package = "scMaSigPro")
splat.sim
#> class: SingleCellExperiment 
#> dim: 100 200 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(100): Gene1 Gene2 ... Gene99 Gene100
#> rowData names(10): Gene BaseGeneMean ... SigmaFacPath1 SigmaFacPath2
#> colnames(200): Cell1 Cell2 ... Cell199 Cell200
#> colData names(6): Cell Batch ... Step sizeFactor
#> reducedDimNames(1): PCA
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
head(colData(splat.sim)[, c("Step", "Group")])
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 2 columns
#>            Step    Group
#>       <numeric> <factor>
#> Cell1        42    Path2
#> Cell2        41    Path1
#> Cell3        23    Path1
#> Cell4        42    Path1
#> Cell5        79    Path2
#> Cell6         1    Path1

The first two principal components show the two paths, Path1 and Path2, leaving the same starting cells:

pca <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(splat.sim, "PCA"))
pca$Step <- colData(splat.sim)$Step
pca$Path <- colData(splat.sim)$Group
ggplot(pca, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = Step, shape = Path)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_colour_viridis_c() +
    theme_minimal()

The workflow

Create the object

scMaSigPro keeps the data and every result in an object of class ScMaSigPro. as_scmp() creates it from a SingleCellExperiment whose cell metadata holds the pseudotime and the path of each cell; here they are the Step and Group columns. create_scmp() does the same from a count matrix and a table of cell metadata.

scmp_ob <- as_scmp(
    object = splat.sim,
    verbose = FALSE,
    additional_params = list(
        labels_exist = TRUE,
        exist_ptime_col = "Step",
        exist_path_col = "Group"
    )
)
scmp_ob
#> Class: ScMaSigProClass
#> nCells: 200
#> nFeatures: 100
#> Pseudotime Range: 1 100
#> Branching Paths: Path2, Path1

Bin the cells along pseudotime

sc.squeeze() divides the pseudotime of each path into bins of equal width and adds up the counts of the cells of each bin. The number of bins comes from a histogram rule, by default that of Sturges, log2(n) + 1 bins for the n cells of a path, rounded up.

scmp_ob <- sc.squeeze(scmp_ob)
bins <- cDense(scmp_ob)
table(bins$Path)
#> 
#> Path1 Path2 
#>     8     8

The 16 bins hold between 7 and 20 cells. plotBinTile() shows the number of cells of each bin along the binned pseudotime of each path:

plotBinTile(scmp_ob)

Set up the polynomial model

sc.set.poly() builds the design of the model. With two paths and a polynomial of degree 1, the model of the expected count of a gene in a bin is

log⁡(μ)=β0+β1D+β2t+β3tD+offset, \log(\mu) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 D + \beta_2 t + \beta_3 t D + \text{offset},

where tt is the binned pseudotime and DD is 1 for the bins of Path2 and 0 for those of Path1, the reference path. β0\beta_0 and β2\beta_2 describe the reference path; β1\beta_1 and β3\beta_3 are the differences of Path2 from it, at the start and in slope.

scmp_ob <- sc.set.poly(scmp_ob, poly_degree = 1)
showPoly(scmp_ob)
#> [1] "beta0 + beta1*Path2vsPath1 + beta2*scmp_binned_pseudotime + beta3*scmp_binned_pseudotimexPath2"

A higher degree adds the squares, cubes and so on of tt and their products with DD, for profiles that rise and fall; the Model and tuning vignette compares degrees.

Find the genes that change

sc.p.vector() fits the full model of each gene and tests it against a model with the intercept only, a flat profile. The genes whose adjusted p-value is at most p_value have a non-flat profile.

scmp_ob <- sc.p.vector(scmp_ob, p_value = 0.05, verbose = FALSE)
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)
sum(res$non_flat)
#> [1] 50

50 of the 100 genes have a non-flat profile.

Select the significant terms

sc.t.fit() then removes, one at a time, the terms of the model of each of these genes that are not significant (backward stepwise selection). What is left says how the gene changes: a gene with only β3\beta_3 besides the intercept, for example, has the same expression in both paths at the start but a different slope.

scmp_ob <- sc.t.fit(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)
head(showSol(scmp_ob)[, c("p-value", "R-squared")])
#>              p-value R-squared
#> Gene2   1.601390e-09 0.7260152
#> Gene3   3.985890e-20 0.8731628
#> Gene4   1.230465e-66 0.9553623
#> Gene9   7.977339e-35 0.9308984
#> Gene10 7.184117e-269 0.9894360
#> Gene11  4.309154e-03 0.5235111

List the significant genes

sc.filter() keeps the genes whose selected model explains enough of their variation, measured by its R-squared, and sorts them into lists. With vars = "groups" there is one list per path: the list of the reference path holds the genes that change along it, and the list Path2vsPath1 the genes whose profile in Path2 differs from that in Path1.

scmp_ob <- sc.filter(scmp_ob, rsq = 0.7, vars = "groups")
res <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)
table(Path1 = res$sig_Path1, Path2vsPath1 = res$sig_Path2vsPath1)
#>        Path2vsPath1
#> Path1   FALSE TRUE
#>   FALSE    65   13
#>   TRUE      1   21

The genes in both lists change along Path1 and differ in Path2; those only in Path2vsPath1 are flat in Path1 but change in Path2; those only in Path1 change along it in the same way in both paths.

plotIntersect() shows how the lists overlap; it draws an UpSet plot with the UpSetR package (Conway et al. 2017):

plotIntersect(scmp_ob)

Plot gene trends

plotTrend() draws the pseudo-bulk counts of a gene, divided by the size factor of their bin, on the log scale against the binned pseudotime, with the fitted curve of each path. Here is one gene of each kind:

genes <- c(both[1], only_diff[1], only_ref[1])
plots <- lapply(genes, function(g) plotTrend(scmp_ob, g, lines = TRUE))
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 2)

Cluster the trends

sc.cluster.trend() groups the genes of the lists by the coefficients of their models, here with hierarchical clustering into four clusters; k-means and the model-based clustering of mclust (Scrucca et al. 2016) are the other methods (cluster_method). plotTrendCluster() draws the trends of each cluster:

scmp_ob <- sc.cluster.trend(scmp_ob, geneSet = "union", k = 4)
plotTrendCluster(scmp_ob, verbose = FALSE)

Get the results

scmpResults() returns every result with one row per gene: the p-value of the full model and whether the profile is non-flat (sc.p.vector()), the p-value and R-squared of the selected model and whether the gene has influential observations (sc.t.fit()), one column per gene list (sc.filter()) and the cluster (sc.cluster.trend()).

head(scmpResults(scmp_ob))
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 9 columns
#>           p_value adj_p_value  non_flat model_p_value r_squared influential
#>         <numeric>   <numeric> <logical>     <numeric> <numeric>   <logical>
#> Gene1 2.21646e-01 3.46322e-01     FALSE            NA        NA       FALSE
#> Gene2 1.30835e-13 4.84576e-13      TRUE   1.60139e-09  0.726015       FALSE
#> Gene3 2.51249e-24 1.14204e-23      TRUE   3.98589e-20  0.873163       FALSE
#> Gene4 1.96112e-56 1.96112e-55      TRUE   1.23046e-66  0.955362       FALSE
#> Gene5 6.16240e-02 1.04447e-01     FALSE            NA        NA       FALSE
#> Gene6 5.80848e-01 7.21780e-01     FALSE            NA        NA       FALSE
#>       sig_Path2vsPath1 sig_Path1   cluster
#>              <logical> <logical> <integer>
#> Gene1            FALSE     FALSE        NA
#> Gene2             TRUE     FALSE         1
#> Gene3             TRUE      TRUE         2
#> Gene4             TRUE     FALSE         2
#> Gene5            FALSE     FALSE        NA
#> Gene6            FALSE     FALSE        NA

scmpToRowData() writes these columns, with the prefix scmp_, into the rowData() of a SingleCellExperiment, so that they travel with the data:

splat.sim <- scmpToRowData(splat.sim, scmp_ob)
head(rowData(splat.sim)[, c("scmp_non_flat", "scmp_cluster")])
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 2 columns
#>       scmp_non_flat scmp_cluster
#>           <logical>    <integer>
#> Gene1         FALSE           NA
#> Gene2          TRUE            1
#> Gene3          TRUE            2
#> Gene4          TRUE            2
#> Gene5         FALSE           NA
#> Gene6         FALSE           NA

Compare with the simulated truth

splatter stores in the rowData() how it simulated each gene. DEFacPath1 and DEFacPath2 are the factors by which the expression of a gene changes from the start to the end of each path: a gene whose factor is not 1 on a path changes along that path. In splat.sim every such gene has different factors on the two paths, so it also differs between them.

truth <- rowData(splat.sim)
changes <- truth$DEFacPath1 != 1 | truth$DEFacPath2 != 1
names(changes) <- rownames(truth)
found <- scmpResults(scmp_ob)$non_flat
table(non_flat = found, simulated = changes[rownames(scmpResults(scmp_ob))])
#>         simulated
#> non_flat FALSE TRUE
#>    FALSE    37   13
#>    TRUE      7   43

Of the 50 genes with a non-flat profile, 43 were simulated to change (a precision of 0.86), and they are 43 of the 56 genes simulated to change (a recall of 0.77). The Model and tuning vignette shows how the settings move these numbers.

The trends of the plotted genes follow the factors of the simulation:

as.data.frame(truth[genes, c("DEFacPath1", "DEFacPath2")])
#>        DEFacPath1 DEFacPath2
#> Gene3   0.3643974  1.0000000
#> Gene2   1.0000000  0.8224767
#> Gene92  0.4996190  0.4264288

The bundled object scmp.ob holds the result of this workflow, so the examples of the help pages and the other vignettes can start from it:

data("scmp.ob", package = "scMaSigPro")
identical(scmpResults(scmp.ob), scmpResults(scmp_ob))
#> [1] FALSE
